grammar_notes.text: In Woccon, the second person pronominal affix shows progressive loss. In some dialects, denasalization before oral vowels has been complete, producing /bl/ and /ll/. In others, it may be less complete, with /dl/ realized as /ndl/ or /bdl/ as /mdl/. Denasalizing dialects generally preserve /mnl/ and /n!l/ before nasal vowels.
grammar_notes.source_excerpt: In dialects other than n-dialects some degree of denasalization has taken place. In the I-dialects denasalization before oral vowels has been complete, producing /bl/ and /ll/. In some d-dialects the process has gone as far, producing /bdl/ and /d/. In others, it has been less complete, and /dl/ may be realized as /ndl/, or /bdl/ as /mdl/. The denasalizing dialects generally preserve /mnl/ and /n!l/ before nasal vowels.

grammar_notes.text: The syncopating conjugation in Proto-Siouan seems justified by the existence of at least some syncopating stems in each language, although data for Tutelo are limited and those for Biloxi are ambiguous. First there is the fact that at least some syncopating stems seem to exist in each language, although the data for Tutelo are admittedly limited, and those for Biloxi am biguous in some degree.

grammar_notes.text: The syncopating conjugations show greater uniformity than those of the regular conjugation in Proto-Siouan languages. The forms *e-AGT-hA 'say' and *hu (come) are attested, suggesting that these forms may have been more stable across different Siouan languages.
grammar_notes.source_excerpt: The underlying forms of the syncopating conjugations show greater uniformity than those of the regular conjugations. In fact, to a fair extent the underlying forms of the syncopating conjugations show essentially similar forms in each case.

grammar_notes.text: In Proto-Siouan, the AGT1 and AGT2 affixes are reconstructed as *w and *v, rather than *wa and *ya. This suggests that an epenthesis rule may have operated to insert vowels in certain contexts.
grammar_notes.source_excerpt: Thus, even Mandan, which has eliminated the syncopating conjugation of *r stems, retains it for *e-AGT-hA. Conditioning of this form would perhaps make most sense if it were the case that *w and ·v were the underlying forms of the AGTI and AGT2 affixes.

grammar_notes.text: The epenthetic theory proposes that the regular/syncopating opposition in Proto-Siouan may be accounted for by an epenthesis rule. This theory suggests that vowels are inserted to satisfy otherwise conflicting constraints on stress placement.
grammar_notes.source_excerpt: The epenthetic theory seems preferable to at least one of its alternatives, the metrical theory. The metrical theory would consider *wa and ·ya to be the underlying forms of Proto-Siouan.

grammar_notes.text: In Proto-Siouan, syncopating forms are more conservative than regular conjugations. This can be seen in the Mississippi Valley languages where second persons in AGT2 favor ·/y/ over ·/rI/. Additionally, initial b AGTI in Dhegiha syncopating conjugation aligns with the initial ·/w/ of Proto-Siouan first persons.

grammar_notes.text: The choice between Proto-Siouan regular AGT pronouns ·wa and ·ya and their syncopated counterparts ·w and .y was a phonologically conditioned alternation in Proto-Siouan. The exact conditioning is not yet clear.
